acceptance_criteria.criterion: ComputeCropCoordinates clamps x and y to [0, 1 - cropSize] for any pointer position.
ShowMask = false hides the four darkening rectangles; the crop boundary rectangle remains visible.
Source = null renders a blank control without throwing.
Drag interaction updates CropX and CropY observable properties on the control.
dotnet build -c Release reports zero warnings.

summary: Implemented CoverImageCropperControl as a new Avalonia UserControl with Grid root containing Image and Canvas overlay.
Defined 5 styled properties: Source (Bitmap?), CropX (float), CropY (float), CropSize (float), ShowMask (bool).
Canvas overlay contains 4 semi-transparent dark mask rectangles (visible when ShowMask=true) and 1 white-bordered crop boundary rectangle (always visible when Source is loaded).
Pointer event handlers (PointerPressed/Moved/Released) implement drag interaction; SetCurrentValue used for CropX/CropY to preserve two-way bindings.
ComputeCropCoordinates internal static pure method clamps to [0, 1-cropSize] and accounts for Stretch.Uniform letter-boxing via ComputeImageBounds.
UpdateOverlay positions all 5 rectangles in pixel coordinates derived from image bounds and normalised crop coordinates.
Release build: 0 warnings, 0 errors. All 643 tests pass (282 unit + 361 app).

comments.note: CoverImageCropperControl.axaml.cs: LayoutUpdated is a per-instance event in Avalonia 11 (fires after each layout pass for this control specifically), which is the right hook for repositioning overlay rects. If profiling reveals overhead, a future optimisation is to override ArrangeOverride and pass finalSize directly to UpdateOverlay to avoid reading Bounds.Size one frame late.

ComputeImageBounds accounts for Stretch.Uniform but does not handle Stretch.None or Stretch.Fill. This is intentional since the Image in the AXAML is hard-coded to Stretch.Uniform, but if the stretch mode ever becomes configurable the helper will need updating.
Drag uses pointer capture (e.Pointer.Capture(this)) to continue receiving PointerMoved events outside the control bounds. This is the correct approach. No issues found.

summary: All 5 acceptance criteria verified by code inspection.
AC1 (clamping): ComputeCropCoordinates uses Math.Clamp(norm, 0f, Math.Max(0f, 1f - cropSize)) on both axes; clampMax guards against negative range when cropSize > 1.
AC2 (ShowMask): All four _mask* rects have IsVisible = showMask; _cropBorder.IsVisible is always set to true when a source is loaded, independent of ShowMask.
AC3 (null Source): UpdateOverlay early-returns hiding all 5 overlay elements when source is null; PointerPressed and PointerMoved handlers guard with 'if (Source is null) return'.
AC4 (drag): ApplyDrag calls SetCurrentValue(CropXProperty, x) and SetCurrentValue(CropYProperty, y) preserving two-way bindings; pointer capture ensures drag continues outside control bounds.
AC5 (build): dotnet build -c Release 0 warnings, 0 errors. 643/643 tests pass.

comments.note: ComputeCropCoordinates correctly handles the edge case when cropSize > 1: clampMax is clamped to 0f (preventing negative clamp range), locking x and y to 0. This is a safe defensive behaviour.

ComputeImageBounds returns the full control Bounds rect when Source is null (instead of a zero-rect). This is used by UpdateOverlay which independently guards on source is null and returns early, so the two guards are complementary and safe.

The control is marked internal for unit testability (ComputeCropCoordinates and ComputeImageBounds are 'internal static'). No unit tests currently exist for these helpers. A future test asserting clamp behaviour for boundary inputs would improve regression safety.

summary: Code review complete — PASS with no changes required.
AXAML: clean Grid+Canvas overlay structure; IsHitTestVisible=False on Canvas is correctly documented; ClipToBounds prevents overflow.
Styled property registration uses correct Avalonia 11 pattern for all 5 properties.
ComputeCropCoordinates: center-on-pointer math correct; degenerate cropSize>1 handled by clamping clampMax to 0; zero-imageBounds guard present.
ComputeImageBounds: Stretch.Uniform letterboxing math correct; all degenerate inputs (null, zero-size) handled.
UpdateOverlay mask math algebraically verified: no overflow possible when crop coordinates are within their clamped range.
SetCurrentValue for drag updates preserves two-way bindings correctly.
LayoutUpdated lambda lifecycle is correct (no memory leak).

comments.note: Styled property registration follows correct Avalonia 11 patterns (AvaloniaProperty.Register<TOwner, TValue>) for all 5 properties. SetCurrentValue used for drag updates — correct two-way binding preservation. Pointer capture on PointerPressed, release on PointerReleased — correct.

UpdateOverlay mask math verified algebraically: since cy is clamped to [0, 1-cropSize], cropTop + cropHeight = img.Y + cy * img.Height + cSize * img.Height <= img.Y + img.Height = img.Bottom. So _maskRight.Height = cropHeight and _maskBottom.Height = img.Bottom - cropBottom are both non-negative within normal crop coordinate bounds. Math.Max(0, ...) guards are additionally defensive but the invariant holds.

ComputeImageBounds fallback on null source returns the full control rect (not a zero rect). This is safe: UpdateOverlay independently guards 'if source is null return' before calling ComputeImageBounds. The two guards are complementary and correct.

LayoutUpdated lambda (_, _) => UpdateOverlay() captures 'this'. Since the control is sealed and the subscription is on the instance's own event, the lambda lifecycle is correctly tied to the control's lifetime. No memory leak.
